acceptance_criteria.criterion: A routed test hostname (curl -H "Host:") returns HTTP 200 with agentflow queue state.
The example config parses and documents the agentflow section.
gofmt -l prints nothing, go vet ./... is clean, and make test passes.
git status --short lists no files outside the allowlist: internal/agentflow/, web/agentflow/, docs/guides/agentflow.md, plus append-only registrations, example JSON, and README sections.
Queue and progress for the configured project are visible through the module endpoint.
No Go or TypeScript fixture duplicates an existing one: every test helper the module uses resolves to an already-present file or shared asset.
The module page renders the shared theme, a working hamburger menu, and a logout button that returns to login.
With the module listed in auth.modules, PIN-gate and LDAP login behave exactly as on other modules, with no module-specific auth code.

constraints: Additive-only outside the new module: no refactors of dispatch, platform/*, or other modules; no behavior change to existing modules.
New files only under internal/agentflow/, web/agentflow/, docs/guides/agentflow.md, plus append-only registrations (knownModules, buildModule case), example JSON section, and README section.
The module must be self-contained: FRD-1 output copied in with import paths rewritten; no build-time dependency on /opt/agentflow.
Do not touch the taskmaster module, other modules, or shared platform code.
Work happens on the agentflow branch; keep the branch merge-clean for the other active branch.
context: Phase 2 of bringing agentflow into unified-webapp as a module, on the agentflow branch (currently clean). Module anatomy to follow: internal/<name>/ with Build(cfg) http.Handler, a config.XConfig plus Config field, a knownModules entry plus buildModule case, web/<name>/ statics, example-JSON plus README plus docs/guides entries. Pre-commit gate is make check with gofmt/go vet run separately. Phase 1 (FRD-101, in /opt/agentflow) produces the clean copy this phase vendors.
objective: Integrate agentflow into unified-webapp as a first-class module so an operator can open the agentflow host and view and drive one project's agentflow run, registered exactly like every other module.

requirements.description: A new internal/agentflow package shall expose Build(cfg config.AgentflowConfig) (http.Handler, error) serving the phase-1 operator surface against a configured project directory and data directory.
A config.AgentflowConfig struct plus Config.Agentflow field, example-JSON section, and README section shall exist, following the TodoConfig pattern.
A knownModules entry and buildModule case shall register the module.
A web/agentflow/ static directory shall be wired as the module static_dir with committed artifacts satisfying web-verify.
A docs/guides/agentflow.md operator guide shall exist.
gofmt -l shall print nothing, go vet ./... shall be clean, and make test shall pass (full make check if the worker environment supports it).

DRY: the module shall consume existing fixtures, helpers, and assets instead of inventing duplicates — Go test fixtures/helpers already present in the repo, and web/shared theme, menu, session, and icon assets (imported as @shared) on the frontend. New fixtures only where none exist.

The module UI shall be theme-compatible via web/shared (ThemeManager, tokens) and include the standard hamburger menu (HamburgerMenu from @shared) and a logout button (shared session logout posting to /api/auth/logout), like all other modules.
The module shall inherit platform authentication with no custom auth code: protection via auth.modules listing, PIN door via pin_file, and LDAP via the shared doors, per the standard module contract.

title: agentflow module in unified-webapp
